Degree Audit
Degree Audit is an advising tool to guides students in their academic
requirements and progress.
While it provides a list of necessary courses, regular meetings with
academic advisors are strongly recommended to ensure timely degree
completion.
It is not intended to replace academic advising – direct questions
regarding Degree Audit to your advisor.
Accessing Degree Audit:
Login to your ConnectOW account
Click on the Degree Audit (DGW) icon in the Applications card
Select Campus: Old Westbury (for the first-time only)
Note: Information is updated daily, so recent changes do not appear
immediately.
3

Degree Audit Header
The header area of your audit details your classification (or class standing by credits),
degree, major and other academic information. Verify the major listed is the one you
intended to pursue.
Your initial GPA at Old Westbury will be a 0.0. While credits transfer, your GPA will be calculated based solely by
grades earned in Old Westbury courses.
Note: The School of Business and Education will use the combined GPA* (GPAs of your previous school + Old
Westbury) for admission purposes.
4

Degree Requirements
The Degree block details the total credits required for
your degree and the components that make up your Old
Westbury degree. General Electives must be tracked by
calculating credits.
You must complete 40 credits of required courses in
residence at Old Westbury, as well as a minimum of 120
or 126 total credits.
Your total credits applied for all sections will include
completed and in progress work by default.
Requirements with:
Green checks indicate completed
Blue semi-circles indicate in progress
Red circles indicate still needed
See Legend section at the bottom of the Worksheet for
additional details and codes.
5

Old Westbury Liberal Education Requirements
SUNY Old Westbury requires all students, regardless of
major, to complete two proficiency requirements, one in
Writing and one in Mathematics.
Students who entered OW prior to Fall 2023 are also
required to fulfill Diversity as part of the local
requirements.
Transfer courses may be used to fulfill these
requirements, but for the Writing Proficiency and Math
Proficiency requirements, a grade of C or better is
required in order for the area to be satisfied. (Transfer
courses will have the grade listed with a T in front of it ex
TC, TA, TCR)
6

General Education
This area defines the SUNY and Old Westbury General Education
requirements that all students need to fulfill in order to graduate.
Courses completed at your previous institution may be counted in this
block, and the course and source of credit will be listed.
If you believe you took a course that fulfills one of the General
Education domains but is not listed, and the domain is not met with
another course, contact transfer
_
credit@oldwestbury.edu with a
syllabus for the course for review.
For students transferring from a SUNY or CUNY institution with an
Associate of Arts or Associate Science degree: this area will show as
satisfied provided that the University has received a final transcript
showing the awarded degree. Remember to send a final transcript from
your previous institution that reflects your final grades and awarded
degree so your evaluation can be updated.
7

Major Requirements
This section defines requirements and residency credits
for the major.
You will find:
your major GPA
course options, if any, for fulfilling requirements
important policies in the “Unment conditions for this
set of requirements” section
Note: Any course not yet fulfilled links to course
descriptions and schedule snapshots, if available. Do not
rely on the schedule seen there; always check in Browse
Classes in Banner SSB.
8

Liberal Arts Requirements
This area identifies and tracks the courses that fulfill
the liberal arts requirement for your major. Many of
the courses in your major requirement section and
general education section will also appear in this
section.
Note: Degree Audit stops counting Liberal Arts credits
once you accumulate the required number of credits
towards this section.
Required Liberal Arts credits:
Bachelor's of Arts (B.A.): 90 credits
Bachelor's of Fine Arts (B.F.A.): 90 credits
Bachelor's of Science (B.S.): 60 credits
Bachelor's of Science in Education (B.S.Ed.): 60 credits
Bachelor’s of Professional Studies (B.P .S): 30 credits
9

Upper Division Requirement
The Upper Division Requirement applies to all students seeking a bachelor’s degree, regardless of major. You
must complete 45 credits of courses numbered 3000 or higher.
Courses that fulfill other requirements can count towards this requirement when they are at or above the
3000-level.
Transfer courses may be used to fulfill this requirement if they are deemed to be at the same level or hold an
Old Westbury equivalent numbered 3000 or higher.
10

Insufficient
Courses that did not satisfy any requirements due to unsatisfactory grades appear in this section.
Fall Through
Courses completed successfully but not applied to other requirements appear in this section.
11

In-progress and Preregistered
Courses that are in-progress and/or preregistered for the upcoming term appear in this section. Since Degree
Audit updates on an overnight cycle, courses you register for will not appear here until the next business day.
Legends
At the bottom of the Audit is the legend that you can use as a quick reference.

Degree Audit What-If Guide
What-If feature
It is a tool to help you decide what major you
would like to declare.
How to use the What-If feature
Under the header box (that contains your ID#,
Name, Major, and other academic information)
click on the gray words “What If”
.
This will open an area where you can select other
majors and minors.
THIS DOES NOT OFFICIALLY CHANGE YOUR
MAJOR.
13

Degree Audit What-If Guide
Click on the drop downs to choose:
Degree
Program
Major
Minor (optional)
Concentration (only for Childhood Ed majors)
Then, click on the gray “Process” button
14

Degree Audit What-If Guide
To return to your original degree audit, click on
the gray word “Academic” above the What-If
Analysis section.
Questions regarding Degree Audit should be
directed to your Academic Advisor or Faculty
Advisor.
15

Degree Audit What-If Guide
How to officially declare a new major
Students can submit the Change of Major Request Form to
declare a new major*
. The form can be found in the Registrar
Forms card in Connect OW.
For declaring a dual major, submit the Dual Major Request
Form instead of the Change of Major Request Form.
How to officially add or remove a minor
Students can submit the Minor Request Form to add or
remove a minor. The form can be found in the Registrar
Forms card in Connect OW.
*Students must meet the admission requirements to declare
a major in the School of Business or Education.
